claim: In experiment, tetrahedrally lobed patchy particles with 1-um polystyrene lobes crystallised into cubic diamond with Pluronic F127 micelles as depletant in 500 mM NaCl at 0.60% (w/v) F127, just above the critical micelle concentration and corresponding to a depletant volume fraction of about 0.03; nothing crystallised at 0.55% (w/v), and above 0.60% the structures grew increasingly dendritic.

numbers.name: depletant_volume_fraction
numbers.note: volume fraction of F127 micelles actually in the sample at the 0.60% (w/v) threshold, explicit depletant, as the paper states it.

validity_conditions: AN EXPERIMENT, NOT A MODEL RESULT. Room temperature, 500 mM NaCl (Debye length 0.43 nm), HMDS-treated glass capillaries of 100 um x 2 mm x 5 cm; the series ran from 0.6% to 0.8% (w/v) F127. The authors attribute the dendritic growth at higher depletion to rapid sticking and kinetic roughening, as in diffusion-limited aggregation. The F127 critical micelle concentration is about 0.1% (w/v). Mass-per-volume percentages are carried in words; the store registers mg/ml but the paper states w/v percent, and no conversion was made.
